title: Graded Nakayama freeness criterion
statement: Let k be a field and S=k[x_0,x_1] with total-degree grading S_d equal to the k-span of monomials of degree d and S_d=0 for d<0 [def-sc-p1-standard], and let S_+=(x_0,x_1). If N is a finitely generated Z-graded S-module and Tor_1^S(N,k)=0 [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], then N is graded free, hence a finite direct sum of graded shifts S(d) [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] (2).

source.place: proof, graded Nakayama criterion applied to K_2

proof.text: By [lem-sc-p1-graded-nakayama-generation], choose a homogeneous k-basis of N/S_+N and homogeneous lifts n_1,...,n_r. The corresponding graded map q:F=direct sum_j S(-deg n_j) \to N is surjective, and its induced map F/S_+F \to N/S_+N is an isomorphism, so q is a minimal finite graded free presentation.

source.place: proof, graded Nakayama criterion applied to K_2

proof.text: Put K=ker(q). The minimal-presentation Tor calculation [lem-sc-p1-minimal-presentation-tor] identifies Tor_1^S(N,k) with K/S_+K. The hypothesis Tor_1^S(N,k)=0 therefore gives K/S_+K=0.

source.place: proof, graded Nakayama criterion applied to K_2

proof.text: The kernel K=ker(q) of the graded surjection q:F \to N between finitely generated graded S-modules is a finitely generated graded S-module by [lem-sc-p1-graded-kernel-finite]. Applying [lem-sc-p1-graded-nakayama-generation] to K and the empty family of homogeneous generators, using K/S_+K=0, yields K=0.

source.place: proof, graded Nakayama criterion applied to K_2

proof.text: Thus q:F \to N is an isomorphism of graded modules. Since F is a finite direct sum of graded shifts S(d) [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] (2), N has the asserted graded-free form.
